To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) semantic data provisioning and reasoning are both possible for IoT, (2) semantic data provisioning is more scalable with a publish-subscribe architecture than with a pull-based approach, (3) reasoning is more scalable when using an ontology-based data access (OBDA) approach than when using a semantic web rule language (SWRL), (4) reasoning over data aggregated at the IoT node is faster than when reasoning over raw data from the sensor
(1) the use of semantic technologies for IoT data management and reasoning is feasible, and (2) the choice of data aggregation strategy has a significant effect on the performance of reasoning.

(1) the performance of semantic data provisioning is significantly affected by data size and the type of reasoning engine, and (2) the performance of reasoning is significantly affected by the data aggregation strategies and the type of the reasoning engine.
